Hi-Tech Lubricants Ltd announces new blending plant to expand production capacity in Pakistan

KARACHI, Pakistan, June 14 — Hi-Tech Lubricants Ltd, a leading player in Pakistan’s chemicals and lubricants sector, announced Friday it will invest PKR 2.3 billion ($8.2 million) in a new blending facility near Lahore, aimed at increasing domestic production and meeting rising demand for industrial and automotive lubricants.

The company said construction of the plant is expected to begin in the third quarter of 2024, with commissioning targeted for late 2025. The facility will have an initial capacity of 45,000 metric tons per year, with potential to expand further based on market needs.

“Our new blending plant reflects our confidence in Pakistan’s growing industrial and transport sectors,” said Shahbaz Arif, Chief Executive Officer of Hi-Tech Lubricants Ltd, in a statement. “This investment will allow us to localize production, reduce lead times, and serve our customers more efficiently across the country.”

Industry analysts welcomed the move, noting that Pakistan’s lubricants market has seen steady growth in recent years, fueled by infrastructure projects and increasing vehicle ownership. “This expansion by Hi-Tech Lubricants Ltd is a positive signal for the chemicals industry, which has shown resilience despite macroeconomic headwinds,” said Saira Khalid, a Karachi-based chemicals analyst.

The new facility will create approximately 120 direct jobs and several hundred indirect opportunities through logistics and support services, according to the company. The plant will also feature automated batching and packaging lines, and will adhere to international quality and environmental standards.

The Pakistan Chemicals Manufacturers Association also praised the announcement. “Investments like this strengthen the domestic supply chain and help reduce reliance on imported products,” said Farooq Malik, the association’s secretary-general.

Shares of Hi-Tech Lubricants Ltd closed up 2.1% on the Pakistan Stock Exchange following the news.
